verdict: Too early to call, and the price isn't in text yet. What the first episode does show is the reason the Niko Brothers keep buying burned RVs: a coach that still runs, drives and cools has its expensive parts (chassis, engine, generator and A/C) intact, and fire damage confined to the interior is mostly labor and materials. Clean 2008 Bounders list for roughly $19,000 to $34,000, so if the buy really was cheap and the melted interior stays cosmetic rather than structural, the numbers can work. If heat got into the walls, roof or wiring, a 2008 coach can easily cost more to fix than it's worth.
body:
## The buy

The Niko Brothers, Mike and Ivan, buy wrecked, flooded and burned vehicles at auction and rebuild them on camera, and motorhomes have become one of their staples [6]. On October 27, 2026 they posted "Burnt RV: We Have Rebuilt One Before, Should We Do It Again?", in which Mike checks out a mini excavator at the local Copart heavy-equipment lot and asks viewers whether it is time for another long-term burnt-RV restoration [1].

Six days later the answer was on the channel. In "I Bought a BURNED RV at Auction for CHEAP… The Inside Is COMPLETELY MELTED!" (November 2), Mike has won a fire-damaged 2008 Bounder at auction and drives it back to the shop [2]. The video's description doesn't name the auction house or where the coach was, and while it promises the total cost in the video, no figure appears in text. Since we can't watch the video, the purchase price in this file is blank rather than guessed.

The Bounder, built by Fleetwood, is one of the best-known gas Class A motorhomes in the U.S. The floor plan of this one hasn't been given.

## The damage

What's on the record is short and mixed. The title says the inside is "COMPLETELY MELTED" [2]. The description says the coach still runs and drives, and that the air conditioning still works [2]. That combination matters: on a motorhome the chassis, engine, transmission, generator and roof air units are the parts that cost real money, and a coach that can be driven home has at least some of them intact.

How the fire started, where it burned and whether heat reached the roof, walls or wiring have not been described in text. Those are the questions that decide whether a burned RV is a rebuild or a parts coach.

## The work and the parts

The rebuild hasn't started on camera, and the brothers haven't itemized anything. The parts list in this file is therefore our estimate of what a melted interior usually needs, each marked as an estimate with no price: wall and ceiling panels; cabinetry, seating and flooring; the coach's 12-volt and 120-volt wiring and fixtures in the burned area; and smoke and odor remediation for everything else. We'll replace it with the brothers' own list as the episodes come.

They have done this before: the October 27 video's title says they have rebuilt a burnt RV already [1]. The channel is also partway through a flood project, a Monaco diesel pusher bought for $21,000 [6].

## The money

In: unknown for now. Out: there's a ceiling. Clean 2008 Bounder 35E coaches are listed at dealers for $18,900 (85,000 miles, since sold or withdrawn) and $34,000 (65,000 miles, the sale price on a $38,900 listing) [3][4]. A fire history, and the branded title that usually comes with an insurance or auction sale, typically takes 20% to 40% off against a clean comparable [5]. On those numbers a properly rebuilt coach would fetch roughly $11,000 to $24,000. That is our estimate, and the comparables are 35E coaches, which may not match this one's floor plan.

So the margin depends on two things the text doesn't tell us yet: what Mike paid, and how far the melting goes. A cheap buy with a cosmetic interior fire can pay; a coach with heat damage in its structure or wiring usually doesn't.

## What's next

The coming episodes should show the stripped interior and the real extent of the fire, and give the purchase price. We'll add the price, the parts and their costs, and the status as the brothers post them.
